harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created `Fleet Internal CA` on node1, issued a certificate for node2, and configured node2 to serve trusted HTTPS at https://10.100.129.11:8443/. The CA is trusted system-wide on both nodes. Both nodes were restarted sequentially and fully recovered with changed boot identities, unchanged OS release/kernel, and persistent TLS functionality.
actions_performed: Installed the signed RHEL OpenSSL tooling only on node1.
Created the CA with a protected 4096-bit private key and critical CA constraints.
Generated node2’s 3072-bit TLS private key locally on node2 and issued a server-auth certificate containing DNS and IP SANs.
Installed the CA in both RHEL system trust stores.
Created an enabled, hardened systemd HTTPS service running under a locked dedicated account on node2.
Opened only TCP/8443 in node2’s runtime and persistent firewalld configuration.
Verified successful trusted HTTPS, TLS-only behavior, and rejection of an incorrect hostname.
Removed temporary transfer artifacts and audited listeners, permissions, failed units, administrative access, release, and kernel state.
Restarted node1 and node2 one at a time and verified changed boot identities plus complete recovery.

evidence.requirement: Create Fleet Internal CA on node1
evidence.summary: Shows the self-signed `CN=Fleet Internal CA`, critical CA constraints/key usage, fingerprint, protected key permissions, and durable CA files.

evidence.requirement: Issue a valid TLS certificate for node2
evidence.summary: Node2 generated its key locally; the issued non-CA certificate chains to Fleet Internal CA, has server-auth usage, and includes `DNS:node2` and `IP:10.100.129.11` SANs.

evidence.requirement: Install the CA as a trusted system authority on both nodes
evidence.summary: Node1’s system bundle verifies the chain, and default-trust curl requests on both nodes return HTTP 200 with `ssl_verify_result=0`, including after restart.

evidence.requirement: Serve HTTPS on node2 port 8443 securely and persistently
evidence.summary: The hardened service runs as `fleet-https`, listens at 10.100.129.11:8443, and has a persistent firewall allowance. TLS 1.3 peer verification succeeds; an incorrect hostname is rejected.

evidence.requirement: Preserve installed OS release, kernel, administrative access, and security controls
evidence.summary: Before/after evidence shows RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 unchanged, SSH active, SELinux retained, expected listeners only, and no failed units or temporary residue.
Captures healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot identity, running system state, unchanged CA data, restored SSH/trust, and successful HTTPS access.
Captures healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered enabled service/listener/firewall, unchanged TLS material, and successful local and remote trusted HTTPS.
